[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey team, quick agenda run-through: adoption, costs, reliability, pilot handoff.
[00:14] Maya Singh: Thanks. we want to be tactical. baseline about 60 qps, experiments spike to 180 qps. long medical notes cause long token sequences.
[00:31] Riya Patel: Can you post a 7-day traffic sample? p50/p95 distributions will help us size batching and cache.
[00:44] Maya: yes we'll share, anonymized. note: many long sequences and repeated prefixes.
[01:02] Carlos Duarte: Our infra only allows VPC peering in scheduled windows; private deploy timing depends on that.
[01:15] Ethan: We can run hosted pilot first then migrate to private. what's your primary SLO?
[01:28] Jin Park: P99 < 350ms for edge path, target cost ~30% lower per call vs our GPUs, and KMS-backed zero data leakage.
[01:43] Riya: For P99 that tight, dedicated capacity often helps. are you comfortable with quantized models if eval delta <1%?
[01:56] Maya: up to 1% is acceptable if validated against our evals.
[02:08] Ethan: We'll send hosted and dedicated pilot pricing and a burst example.
[02:20] Riya: KV cache + prefix caching can drop token spend substantially; i'll run a micro-benchmark on your sample.
[02:34] Carlos: when you say KV cache, some docs call it K V cash, so that's been confusing for our infra notes.
[02:45] Riya: yeah transcription hits that sometimes. it's the keyed-value cache for decoder-side reuse.
[02:57] Jin: We need SOC2, encryption details, and a Vault KMS integration template.
[03:08] Ethan: We'll send the security pack with SOC2, SAML/SCIM notes, and KMS options including Vault guidance.
[03:22] Maya: timeline — if we get configs and pricing this week we can kick off mid-Jan for six weeks.
[03:33] Riya: Pilot plan: canary latency check, ramp to 100 qps, then stress to 150-200 qps. week 3 add regional failover test.
[03:48] Carlos: cost ballpark for 150 qps mixed short/long prompts?
[03:57] Riya: ballpark: with batching and cache, 20-40% lower cost per 1k tokens depending on hit rate and quantization; we'll provide a spreadsheet.
[04:11] Jin: customers ask about Bedrock and vendor lock — how do you position Redwood?
[04:21] Ethan: We emphasize production economics, unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, rollouts and routing, and easy migration to private without code changes.
[04:36] Maya: fallback behavior — can requests automatically go to smaller models if a region is saturated?
[04:45] Riya: Yes, routing policies allow latency-first then cost-aware fallback to quantized or smaller variants. canary rules and A/B supported.
[04:58] Ethan: For your front-line endpoints, dedicated reserved slots plus hosted for background looks best.
[05:08] Carlos: network requirements for dedicated?
[05:15] Riya: baseline VPC egress and peering required; we'll document ports, IP ranges, and peering windows.
[05:28] Maya: we also need per-route token breakdowns and tracing for debugging.
[05:34] Jordan Lee: console provides per-route token/latency breakdowns, traces, and alert hooks; i'll include screenshots.
[05:47] Ethan: Recap next steps: pricing + spreadsheet, SE benchmarks, traffic sample + SLOs, security pack + KMS guidance, pilot kickoff invite.
[05:59] Maya: sounds good.
[06:05] [end recording omitted]
